newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Travel buys HK$910 mln hotel asset.
newsitem.headline: China Travel buys HK$910 mln hotel asset.

text.p: China Travel International Investment Hong Kong Ltd has agreed to buy Metropole Hotel in Hong Kong from its 66.47 percent controlling parent China Travel Service (Holdings) Hong Kong Ltd for a total of HK$910 million, China Travel International said in a statement on Tuesday.
It said it would fund the purchase with internal resources.
The purchase price represented a 44.8 percent discount to an open market valuation of the Metropole Hotel at HK$1.65 billion by independent property valuer 10 days ago, the statement said.

China Travel International said it would buy the hotel through a reorganisation of share capital, which would result in the company owning Hotel Metropole Holdings Ltd, the company which until now wholly owned Metropole Hotel.

Metropole Hotel is located at 75 Waterloo Road in Kowloon with a total gross floor area of 20,217 sq. metres. The 487-room hotel is in the category of medium tariff hotel according to the classifications of the Hong Kong Tourist Association.
The company's chairman Zhu Yuening said the purchase would provide synergy to the company's existing hotel business, enhancing its asset base and enlarging its reserve.
The purchase is conditional on shareholders' approval, it said.

China Travel International engages in the operation of tours and hotels,, provision of freight forwarding and transport services, operation of three theme parks in Shenzhen and industrial investment in China.

In August, China Travel International's parent placed 284.48 million shares at HK$2.088 per share with professional investors before it subscribed 379.31 million new shares at the same price. It said proceeds would be used to fund asset purchases.
Its shares ended at HK$2.30 on Monday, up HK$0.05.
